title: Model ingress surge & KV footprint worksheet
body:
Purpose:
Quick working worksheet to estimate KV cache memory pressure and GPU headroom for the planned inbound-wave launch of the new 30B-compat model (internal name: ember-30B). This is intentionally a lightweight spreadsheet-style analysis for the infra launch runbook — not the final sizing doc.

Context / why this matters:
- Ember-30B will be served in all regions with automatic routing. It has 2x longer average context usage vs current baseline models for our playground and product traffic.
- KV cache is host-device hybrid: we keep the active KV partitions in GPU DRAM when possible (fast path) but overflow/backing stored in local host RAM and NVMe. The cost and latency tradeoff depends on active working set.
- We need conservative regional headroom for a 48-hour wave during onboarding (gradual traffic ramp, plus spikes).

Assumptions (input parameters - edit as experiments run):
- Model weight size (quantized) on disk: 60 GB (sharded across 2 GPUs per replica).
- Serving GPU options: A100-40GB (legacy), H100-80GB (preferred).
- Average request pattern for wave (global): 4.5M requests/day -> ~52 req/s sustained, but surge windows up to 3x sustained for short periods.
- Average generation tokens per request (user+assistant): 120 tokens (median) for product flows; playground can go higher.
- KV per token in fast-path (device-resident) = 12 KB/token (this is conservative; includes key+value for all layers in current runtime encoding).
- KV stored in host RAM (if spilled) has ~30% extra overhead due to indexing structures/index shards.
- Admission target p99 latency depends on device-resident KV; we aim to keep >= 70% of working set device-resident in each region for p99 SLO.
- Replica concurrency (requests served in-flight per replica at p99): 16 for ember-30B (with batching).

Quick formulas used in sheet (copy into any cell):
- per_session_kv_mb = (avg_tokens * kv_kb_per_token) / 1024
- region_working_set_mb = per_session_kv_mb * concurrent_active_sessions_in_region
- device_kv_headroom_needed_gb = region_working_set_mb * target_device_fraction / 1024
- replicas_needed_for_kv = ceil(device_kv_headroom_needed_gb / device_free_kv_capacity_gb_per_replica)

Baseline parameters (editable):
- avg_tokens = 120
- kv_kb_per_token = 12
- global_sustained_rps = 52
- regional_split = {us-east: 45%, eu-west: 35%, ap-south: 20%} (use as guidance)
- concurrency_per_replica = 16
- target_device_fraction = 0.7 (70% of working set device-resident)
- device_free_kv_capacity_gb_per_replica: H100-80GB -> 28 GB free for KV after model weights; A100-40GB -> 6 GB free

Scenarios (run these numbers through the formulas):

1) Optimistic (steady ramp, warm caches)
- sustained rps (global): 52 -> regional us-east: 23.4 rps, eu-west: 18.2 rps, ap-south: 10.4 rps
- expected concurrent active sessions (approx) = regional_rps * avg_latency_window_seconds / 1 (assume avg latency window 6s) => us-east ~140 conc, eu-west ~110, ap-south ~62
- per_session_kv_mb = (120 * 12) / 1024 = 1.40625 MB/session
- region_working_set_mb: us-east ~197 MB, eu-west ~154 MB, ap-south ~87 MB
- device_kv_target (70%): us-east 138 MB (~0.135 GB), eu-west 108 MB (~0.105 GB), ap-south 61 MB (~0.06 GB)
- replicas needed just for device KV headroom: trivial (<<1) on H100; on A100 some pressure but still <1 replica.
- Conclusion: optimistic steady-state is low-pressure for KV on H100s; host spill will be rarely needed.

2) Baseline launch (3x short surge windows, partial warmup)
- burst rps (3x): global 156 rps -> us-east 70 rps, eu-west 55 rps, ap-south 31 rps
- assume avg latency window grows to 8s under burst -> concurrent sessions: us-east 560, eu-west 440, ap-south 248
- per_session_kv_mb unchanged = 1.40625 MB
- region_working_set_mb: us-east ~787 MB (~0.77 GB), eu-west ~618 MB (~0.60 GB), ap-south ~348 MB (~0.34 GB)
- device_kv_target (70%): us-east 550 MB (~0.54 GB), eu-west 433 MB (~0.42 GB), ap-south 244 MB (~0.24 GB)
- device_free_kv_capacity_gb_per_replica: H100 -> 28 GB, A100 -> 6 GB
- required H100 replicas to hold device fraction: us-east 1, eu-west 1, ap-south 1 (very small fraction of a single replica)
- but note: model weight consumes majority of GPU DRAM; these numbers indicate KV alone isn't the scaling limiter in the short burst for H100; however concurrency and batching limits mean we may need more replicas to keep p99 latency low.

3) Worst-case (cold start + cache miss amplification + user sessions longer than expected)
- effective avg_tokens = 400 (some playground flows + heavy contexts), short spike 4x baseline rps -> global 208 rps
- concurrent sessions (assume latency window 12s) and region split -> us-east 1,680 conc, eu-west 1,320, ap-south 744
- per_session_kv_mb = (400 * 12) / 1024 = 4.6875 MB/session
- region_working_set_mb: us-east ~7,875 MB (~7.69 GB), eu-west ~6,187 MB (~6.04 GB), ap-south ~3,487 MB (~3.41 GB)
- device_kv_target (70%): us-east ~5.4 GB, eu-west ~4.2 GB, ap-south ~2.4 GB
- replicas required to keep 70% resident on H100 (28 GB per replica): us-east 1 (fits), eu-west 1 (fits), ap-south 1 (fits) — still fits on H100 but now other constraints (batching, max inf concurrent threads) bind. On A100 (6 GB free) these numbers imply: us-east needs ~1 replica (7.69GB -> device fraction 5.4GB -> requires ~1.0 / A100 is insufficient), actually A100 would need ceil(5.4 / 6) = 1 replica but model weights plus KV may exceed 40GB. In practice A100 fleet will not be able to host this model without spilling and will see increased NVMe/host load.

Regional impacts & operational flags:
- H100 regions: safe headroom for KV in all scenarios; main scaling challenges are CPU bottlenecks for pre/post, admission controller limits, and global network egress for partial KV replication during warmup.
- A100 regions: acceptable for baseline and optimistic, risk in worst-case; plan to limit concurrency, force host-spill policy earlier, or bias traffic to H100 pool during wave.
- APAC: lower absolute numbers but higher variability; recommend a light cold-warm strategy (preseed) 4 hours before wave.

Warmup / pre-seed strategy (recommended practice):
- Shadow traffic: 5% of anticipated wave rps for 1 hour prior to wave start. This pre-populates KV for the most frequent prefixes.
- Seed lists: product team to provide top 10k prefixes (playground + product) to precompute prefix KV and store in region-local object store.
- Staggered start: bring up 20% of launch traffic to H100 pool, verify p99 and KV residency, then open ramps to 60%, then full. Use canary policy per region with automatic fallback to smaller model variant if admission queue grows.

Operational runbook highlights (actionable):
- T-24h: Confirm H100 node availability in us-east and eu-west; mark A100 clusters as "spill-prone" for scheduler.
- T-6h: Start 5% shadow traffic in each region, run KV heavy tracer (script: infra/kv/traces/seed_and_check.sh).
- T-1h: Verify per-region device-resident fraction >= 50% for hot prefixes. If <50%, pause ramp and increase H100 capacity or lower user concurrency.
- During wave: Monitor metrics (dashboard ids) -> kv/device_resident_fraction, kv/host_spill_rate, gpu/p99_latency, admission/queue_depth, replica/active_shards. Keep a run-of-play timeline and escalate at set thresholds.

Mitigations if KV pressure exceeds thresholds:
- Immediate: reduce allowed max generation length by 20% via routing policy for non-critical shards.
- Short term (minutes): divert spawn traffic to smaller model variant (ember-7B) for non-enterprise tenants.
- Medium term (hours): spin additional H100 replicas in region; apply preemption policy on batch jobs where possible.
- Long term: re-evaluate kv_kb_per_token (work with runtime team to compress KV encoding), or implement kv sharding with LRU eviction tuned for sessions.

Open questions / TODOs (owner: Asha):
- Confirm exact kv_kb_per_token for ember-30B on current runtime build (PR #678 had changes). Need runtime bench to validate; ticket INFRA-2143 opened.
- We need a quick microbench to quantify host-spill latency tail for 1GB, 5GB, 10GB host reads. (Action: SRE / observability)
- Product team to provide top 10k prefixes (deadline T-48h).
- Do we want to pre-allocate dedicated NVMe partition for KV spill to avoid I/O interference with other workloads? (ops decision)

Appendix: quick numeric summary (baseline/burst/worst) in GB device-kv-target per region:
- US-EAST: baseline 0.14 GB | burst 0.55 GB | worst 5.4 GB
- EU-WEST: baseline 0.11 GB | burst 0.42 GB | worst 4.2 GB
- AP-SOUTH: baseline 0.06 GB | burst 0.24 GB | worst 2.4 GB

Notes / references:
- See runtime notes: github PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/678 for kv packing changes.
- Deck: Confluence Model Launch Checklist linked above.
- Slack threads: #infra-ember-30b for live chat and quick decisions.

Record of edits / quick changelog (work-in-progress):
- 2026-02-15: initial draft with baseline numbers (Asha)
- 2026-02-20: tightened kv_kb_per_token after quick bench (Liam)
- 2026-03-01: added worst-case scenario and operational runbook (Sofia)

Unresolved: exact serialization overhead in host spill paths and the final desired device-resident fraction for enterprise SLOs (should we require 80%?).

---
This sheet is intentionally compact. Paste numbers into a canonical Google Sheet (infra/capacity/ember-30b-wave) and use live metrics to re-run scenarios before each regional ramp.
